eftersøgt.explanation: "Eftersøgt" means "wanted", as in a person or thing that people are looking for. It comes from the verb "at eftersøge" (to search for): "Politiet eftersøger tyven" (The police are searching for the thief). When many people want to hire someone, it also means "in demand": "en eftersøgt ekspert" (an expert in demand).

eftertragtet.explanation: "Eftertragtet" means "sought-after". It comes from the verb "at tragte efter" (to strive for): "Han tragter efter magt" (He strives for power).

egen.explanation: "Egen" means "own". To say you did something without help, use the phrase "på egen hånd" (by yourself): "Jeg gjorde det på egen hånd" (I did it by myself).

egentlig.explanation: "Egentlig" means "actually". To say the plan was different from what happened, say: "Jeg skulle egentlig arbejde, men jeg er syg" (I was supposed to be working, but I am sick). To ask something you have been wondering about, put it at the end: "Hvad hedder du egentlig?" (What is your name, actually?)

egnet.explanation: "Egnet" means "suitable". To name the person or purpose, add "til" (for): "Filmen er egnet til børn" (The film is suitable for children).

egoistisk.explanation: "Egoistisk" means "selfish". To say the opposite, use "uselvisk" (unselfish): "en uselvisk hjælper" (an unselfish helper).

ejendele.explanation: "Ejendele" means "belongings". To tell someone to bring their things, say: "Tag dine ejendele med" (Take your belongings with you). Do not mix it up with "en ejendom" (a property): "Ejendommen er til salg" (The property is for sale).

ejendommelig.explanation: "Ejendommelig" means "peculiar". When you say a feature belongs to a place, add "for" (for): "Dialekten er ejendommelig for egnen" (The dialect is characteristic of the area). Here it means "characteristic".

eksisterende.explanation: "Eksisterende" means "existing". It comes from the verb "at eksistere" (to exist). To set it against "ny" (new), say: "nye og eksisterende kunder" (new and existing customers).

eksklusiv.explanation: "Eksklusiv" means "exclusive". When you give a price without tax, it means "excluding": "100 kr. eksklusiv moms" (100 kr. excluding VAT). "Moms" (VAT) is the Danish sales tax.

eksport.explanation: "En eksport" means "an export". To name the goods you export, add "af" (of): "eksport af maskiner" (export of machines).

ekstra.explanation: "Ekstra" means "extra". To make a word stronger, put "ekstra" before it: "ekstra god" (extra good).

ekstraordinær.explanation: "Ekstraordinær" means "extraordinary". To praise something far better than normal, say: "en ekstraordinær præstation" (an extraordinary achievement). To say something is outside the normal schedule, say: "et ekstraordinært møde" (an extraordinary meeting).

ekstrem.explanation: "Ekstrem" means "extreme". To say "extremely", use the form "ekstremt": "Det er ekstremt koldt" (It is extremely cold).

ekstremt.explanation: "Ekstremt" means "extremely". To say something is more than "meget" (very), put it before the word: "Det var ekstremt svært" (It was extremely hard).

elegant.explanation: "Elegant" means "elegant". To say someone moves gracefully, add it to the verb: "Hun danser meget elegant" (She dances very elegantly). To praise a clever answer, say: "en elegant løsning" (an elegant solution).

elektricitet.explanation: "Elektricitet" means "electricity". To say the power is out, use "strøm" (power): "Strømmen er gået" (The power is out).

elektrisk.explanation: "Elektrisk" means "electric". To say there is no power, use "strøm" (power): "Der er ingen strøm" (There is no power).

elektronik.explanation: "Elektronik" means "electronics". It is used without an article: "Jeg sparer op til ny elektronik" (I am saving up for new electronics).

elendig.explanation: "Elendig" means "terrible". To say you feel terrible, say: "Jeg har det elendigt" (I feel terrible). To say a person is very bad at something, say: "Han er en elendig sanger" (He is a terrible singer).

eller.explanation: "Eller" means "or". To check that someone agrees, add it at the end of a question: "Du kommer, eller?" (You are coming, right?). Do not mix it up with "ellers" (otherwise): "Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent" (Hurry up, or we will be late).

ellers.explanation: "Ellers" means "or else". When you ask for more, it means "else": "Hvem ellers?" (Who else?). Do not mix it up with "eller" (or), which joins two choices: "te eller kaffe" (tea or coffee).

elleve.explanation: "Elleve" means "eleven". To say "eleventh", use "elvte": "den elvte maj" (May eleventh).

elvte.explanation: "Elvte" means "eleventh". It comes from the number "elleve" (eleven). To use the other spelling, write "ellevte": "den ellevte maj" (May eleventh).

empati.explanation: "Empati" means "empathy". Do not mix it up with "medlidenhed" (pity), which is feeling sorry for someone: "Jeg har medlidenhed med hende" (I feel pity for her).
